metadata.note: Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia (the 'TAG Route') and its predecessor the Chattanooga Southern: one ~92-mile main line, Chattanooga (Union Depot, via the NC&StL to Cravens and Alton Park) - St. Elmo - Flintstone GA - Cenchat - Cooper Heights - Kensington - Estelle (tunnel at the north end of Pigeon Mountain) - McLemore's Cove - Menlo GA - Chesterfield AL - Blue Pond - Yellow Creek - Gadsden AL. NOT the Alabama Great Southern (Trenton, Valley Head), which parallels it to the west. Three features share one trace (Rule 4 split at 1 Feb 1911): Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia Chattanooga - Gadsden 1911-1951; Chattanooga Southern Chattanooga - Gadsden 1893-1910; Chattanooga Southern Chattanooga - Cooper Heights 1891-1892 (north 18 mi of the same trace). Not splits: the 1892-96 receivership/reorganization (Railway -> Railroad), the 1922 receivership (Railroad -> Railway), the 1929 stock purchase, the 1937 re-incorporation, and the 1970/71 Southern Railway stock control (twenty years after passengers ended). Not drawn (Rule 1): freight after 1951; the Coe, Round Mountain and Hillsdale branches and the Owl Hollow and Estelle mine spurs (no confirmed passenger year); the Chickamauga & Durham coal line from Cenchat (a Central of Georgia road). No horsecars (Rule 5). Colours #9B2D5A (TAG) and #3C7A6E (Chattanooga Southern) are new to the dataset.
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap, traced with opstrace.py on 2026-11-10 over the ways tagged old_railway_operator='Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia' (railway=abandoned, name='Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia Railway'; main pieces ways 1562628499 Estelle - Menlo and 7661842 Menlo - Blue Pond, 1009283179 into Gadsden) and old_railway_operator='TAG;NS' (railway=disused, Alton Park - Kensington, the piece operated as the Chattooga & Chickamauga until 2009). Chattanooga end: the L&N-tagged abandoned 'Alton Park Lead' (ways 590242890, 1193822679, 396467752/53/55, 727910318) from Alton Park to the NC&StL at Cravens, about 0.4 mi of the NC&StL (old_railway_operator=L&N, note NC&StL) and an untagged abandoned way (1295490002) running north-east from the NC&StL toward the Union Depot site. The maps.mail.ru Overpass mirror answered only intermittently (504s and dispatcher errors), so instead of opstrace's degree tiles the corridor's railway=*, operator-tagged and abandoned/trail ways were read in three bbox queries (lat 33.97-35.08, lon -86.06..-85.2) and fed to opstrace as extra files. OpenHistoricalMap was queried for the same boxes; its only usable way (Atack 1826-1911 dataset, way 202210126) stood in for 2.3 mi south of Menlo on a first run but is coarser than OSM way 7661842, which covers the same stretch, so OHM was left out of the final trace. Nominatim checks: 'Blue Pond, Alabama' -> Calhoun County (wrong; re-queried with Cherokee County), 'High Point', 'Hillsdale' and 'Rock Creek, Georgia' -> wrong places (not used), 'Menlo' and 'Gadsden' -> administrative areas (Menlo's point lies 0.1 km from the grade and was kept; the Gadsden end is pinned to the south end of TAG way 1009283179).
metadata.not_yet_sourced: (1) TAG passenger END: drawn to 1951 on two secondary sources (chicagorailfan.com; hmdb.org marker 114744, known only from a search summary) with the Feb 1952 Official Guide (table dated December 1951, 'Freight Service only') as a cap; no day or month found. The last year confirmed by a dated timetable/guide listing is 1947 (Fowler '1947G') - the strict fallback is 1911-1947 [OPEN]. Next: Chattanooga Times / Gadsden Times 'last run of the scooter' story, ICC/state commission discontinuance. (2) Chattanooga Southern START: through service drawn from 1893, the first year an Official Guide proves it; whether through trains ran 1891-92 is unknown, and 1890 to Rock Creek (Fowler '(tm)') is left off. The Chattanoogan's 'passenger service only after a few years' conflicts with Fowler. (3) Frequency before 1929 and after 1942 not read; headway 1440 is an estimate outside those tables, and the 1920s steam-vs-motor-car question (2-8-0 no. 201 of 1924 'for passenger service') is unresolved. (4) When Chattanooga Southern trains moved from the Georgia Avenue depot to Union Depot. (5) Any 1892-95 receivership interruption - none found, none assumed. (6) Coe branch passenger status (Fowler '1919G pass?') vs abandonment 1915/1920.

properties.geometry_quality: Chattanooga - Gadsden: traced 91.6 mi (91.6 after Douglas-Peucker 8 m; 92.1 mi before) against 91.7 mi documented Union Depot - Gadsden (May 1929 TAG passenger table via american-rails.com; same figure in Fowler's Georgia list) and 93 mi (railga.com, Chattanooga Southern). Mileposts on the trace check against Fowler: Moons 9.4 (doc 9.5), Cooper Heights 18.5 (doc 18.2), Wilsonia 83.3 (doc 83.4). Miles by source before simplification: {"TAG (OSM old_railway_operator)": 87.8, "(untagged)": 2.1, "Alton Park Lead (L&N-tagged, the TAG's Cravens connection)": 1.6, "NC&StL (joint approach, Union Depot - Cravens)": 0.4, "(connector)": 0.3}. No straight-line legs; the 0.3 mi of '(connector)' is opstrace's <300 m joins between OSM way ends. NOT DRAWN: the last ~0.5 mi into the Chattanooga Union Depot site (Broad St at 9th St) - the depot (demolished 1973) and its approach are lifted and not in OSM, so the line stops at the north-east end of the mapped abandoned approach way; this matches the Western and Atlantic / NC&StL layers, which also stop short of the Union Station site. The untagged abandoned way 1295490002 used for the approach is attributed to the NC&StL's Union Depot line by position and direction only. ALIGNMENT ERA (Rule 2): (a) Chattanooga Southern trains first terminated at the Georgia Avenue depot and only later used Union Depot (Chattanoogan, 2016; date of the change not found), so for the early Chattanooga Southern years the Union Depot approach drawn here is later than the era; (b) Alton Park - Kensington is drawn on the track as it stood when freight-only to 2009 (OSM disused); no relocation is known on it, but none was checked against a period map; (c) the Yellow Creek crossing near Bristow is drawn on OSM's abandoned way across Weiss Lake (the grade was flooded in 1961); (d) the Cravens - Alton Park connection is drawn on the L&N-tagged Alton Park Lead, which the report says is where TAG trains left the NC&StL (Cravens, mi 2.0) - the drawn Cravens junction sits at trace mi 1.5. Mine spurs and the Coe, Round Mountain and Hillsdale branches are not drawn (no passenger evidence).

segments.note: Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia Railroad passenger trains, Chattanooga Union Depot - Alton Park - Flintstone - Kensington - Menlo - Blue Pond - Gadsden, from the consolidation of the Chattanooga Southern (articles dated 10 Jan 1911, effective 1 Feb 1911) - the same line and, as far as found, the same trains under a new name (feature split here per Rule 4). Fowler cites a 1911 TAG company public timetable for many stations. Steam; Ten-Wheelers 8 and 9 (1916) were the last new passenger-type engines (american-rails). Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE carried back from the one-train-each-way 1929 and 1942 tables; no 1911-1921 frequency was read.
sources: Segment-level: start from american-rails.com (ICC-valuation-style corporate dates: articles 10 Jan 1911, effective 1 Feb 1911) and Fowler's '1911t' citations (branchline.uk Georgia list, table 131), as read in research/branches/tennessee_alabama_and_georgia_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the tracer did not re-open these pages. Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia Railway (receivership sale April 1922; new Delaware corporation of the same name 1937 - same operation, not a split). May 1929 table: Train No. 1 Chattanooga Union Depot 7:45am -> Gadsden 11:30am, No. 2 Gadsden 1:00pm -> Chattanooga 4:45pm, 'both daily motor cars', 91.7 mi (american-rails.com). 1942 Chattanooga timetable: No. 1 out 7:55am, No. 2 in 5:00pm, from Union Station (chicagorailfan.com). Fowler cites the 1944 and 1947 Official Guides for Burgess and Congo. A historical marker reportedly says the 'scooter' motor car handled passenger service 1922-1951 (hmdb.org 114744, known only from a search summary). CONFLICT: railga.com says 2-8-0 no. 201 (1924) was built for passenger service (sold 1935), so the motor car may not have been the only passenger equipment 1922-35. END: 1951 rests on two secondary sources (chicagorailfan.com 'Passenger service discontinued in 1951'; the marker, not read directly); no day or month was found. The Feb 1952 Official Guide's TAG table, dated December 1951, prints the stations as 'Freight Service only', which caps service at December 1951 at the latest. The last year confirmed by a dated timetable or guide listing is 1947 (Fowler '1947G'); if the secondary 1951 statements are not accepted, the strict fallback is 1947 [OPEN]. Freight continued (Southern stock control 1971; middle abandoned early 1980s; Chattanooga - Kensington as the Chattooga & Chickamauga to 2009) - not drawn (Rule 1). Headway 1440 min matches the 1929 and 1942 tables; carrying it across 1922-1951 is an estimate.
sources: Segment-level: 1929 and 1942 tables and the 1951 end from american-rails.com and chicagorailfan.com as read in research/branches/tennessee_alabama_and_georgia_railway.txt (researched 2026-11-10); the 1951 end is secondary-source only (hmdb.org marker 114744 was NOT read directly). The December 1951 'Freight Service only' cap was re-read by the tracer in research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt. Headway is an estimate outside 1929 and 1942.
research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt lines ~20807-20865 (TAG table, 'Freight Service only', December 1951)

segments.note: Chattanooga Southern Railway (receiver from 19 Jan 1892; foreclosure 14 Feb 1895) and Chattanooga Southern Railroad (reorganized 10 Jan 1896) - the same property and trains, not a split. Through passenger service Chattanooga - Gadsden is first proven by the 1893 Official Guide (Fowler's 'z' letter on Blanche, Cox's and Wilson's/Wilsonia). 1893 is the first CONFIRMED year, not a known start: construction to Gadsden finished 10 Jun 1891 (american-rails), so through trains may have run in 1891-92, but no source shows it - do not extend without evidence. The 1894 Official Railway List shows 6 passenger cars (railga). CONFLICT: the Chattanoogan (2016) says the road was meant for freight and added passenger service only 'after a few years'; Fowler's dated guide letters are followed. Ends 1910 because the company became the Tennessee, Alabama and Georgia on 1 Feb 1911 - not a cessation. Headway 1440 min is an ESTIMATE carried back from the 1929/1942 one-train-each-way pattern; no Chattanooga Southern frequency was read (railga's 1894, 1895 and 1906 timetable images are broken links).

Headway is an estimate.

segments.note: Chattanooga Southern Railway trains on the north end while construction went on to Gadsden: Fowler's Georgia list gives 'Parks 1891G' (Moons, mi 9.5) and 'Summit 1891G' (Cooper Heights, mi 18.2) from the 1891 Official Guide, so this span is drawn only as far as Cooper Heights.
